Travel times to facilities over a friction surface

Source: R/08-calc_travel_time.R
calc_travel_time.Rd

Computes least-cost travel time from each facility to every non-missing cell of an analysis grid, by accumulating friction (time per unit distance) along the cheapest path between neighboring cells with terra::costDist(). The result is continuous, with no isochrone bands, and can be passed directly to prepare_allocation() as its travel matrix.

Usage

calc_travel_time(
  friction,
  facilities,
  template,
  ids,
  mask = NULL,
  buffer = 50000,
  max_time = Inf,
  method = c("bilinear", "average"),
  type = c("matrix", "raster")
)

Arguments

friction

A one-layer SpatRaster of positive travel time per unit of map distance (for example minutes per metre). Missing cells are barriers; zero or negative values are refused.

facilities

An sf or SpatVector of facility points.

template

A one-layer SpatRaster with square cells in a projected coordinate reference system with map units of metres. Its non-missing cells are the origins.

ids

Name of the facility ID column. The IDs must be unique and nonmissing; they name the columns (or layers) of the result.

mask

Optional polygons (sf or SpatVector); friction outside them is a barrier.

buffer

Distance in map units by which the working grid extends beyond the template (default 50 km).

max_time

Travel times above this value become unreachable: Inf in the matrix (an absent edge for prepare_allocation()) and NA in the raster.

method

How friction is transferred to the template lattice: "bilinear" (default) when the template is about as fine as the friction surface, or "average" when it is coarser, so that fast cells such as roads are averaged rather than sampled.

type

"matrix" (default) for an origin-by-facility matrix whose row names are template cell numbers, or "raster" for one layer per facility.

Value

For type = "matrix", a numeric matrix with a cell_index attribute giving the template cell of each row, so that spatial = list(template = template, cell_index = attr(x, "cell_index")) can be passed to prepare_allocation(). For type = "raster", a SpatRaster on the template grid.

Details

The friction surface is projected to the grid's lattice, extended by buffer so that routes can leave the analysis area, and cells outside mask are treated as barriers (for example, to keep routes within one country). Global motorized friction surfaces, such as those of the Malaria Atlas Project, give minutes per metre; the travel times are then in minutes. The function downloads nothing.

Times are measured between cell centers; the facility's own cell has time zero. Paths that leave the facility cell diagonally are underestimated by at most about a fifth of one cell crossing. Because paths move between neighboring cells in eight directions, travel over uniform friction exceeds the straight-line time by up to about 8%.

See also

Other experimental allocation workflow: bootstrap_allocation(), calc_demand(), check_allocation(), clm_allocation(), compare_allocations(), decay_kernel(), evaluate_allocation(), fit_allocation(), predict_allocation(), prepare_allocation()

Examples

library(sf)
#> Linking to GEOS 3.12.1, GDAL 3.8.4, PROJ 9.4.0; sf_use_s2() is TRUE
library(terra)

# Cornwall population grid in British National Grid (metres)
pop <- project(read_spax_example("cornwall_pop.tif"), "EPSG:27700")

# A uniform friction surface of 50 km/h, in minutes per metre
friction <- init(pop, 60 / 50000)

# Minutes from five practices to every populated cell
gp <- cornwall_gp[1:5, ]
travel <- calc_travel_time(friction, gp, pop, ids = "practice", buffer = 5000)
summary(travel[, 1])
#>    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
#>    0.00   25.54   45.03   47.18   67.17  134.35
